context: Move auto-merge enablement off PR creation. Candidates: enable on ready_for_review rather than opened, so make pr-open creates a draft and the author flips it when the work is actually complete; or have make pr-open enable auto-merge only when explicitly asked (--auto), defaulting off; or keep enablement at open but have auto-merge-on-open.yml withhold until a marker is cleared. Weigh against the must-preserve from pr-open-auto-merge-partial-stack-race-20260804: an ordinary finished PR should still merge hands-free without extra ceremony. Draft-by-default is likely the smallest change that removes the exposure while keeping the hands-free path for finished work.
description: Detection is not enough. make pr-open enables squash auto-merge at PR creation, so any PR that later receives a commit - a review fix, a second unit of work - can merge carrying only its first commit while the rest is still being pushed. Three occurrences in one session: #1503 lost the browser gate job its own PR body described; #1521 and #1531 then each lost the very commit that addressed their Codex review findings, and neither fix reached develop. PR #1521 added per-push orphan detection and PR #1534 re-landed the strandings, but detection is after the fact - #1534 exists only because the detector was run by hand. The exposure is structural: every PR that gets review feedback is a candidate, and review feedback is the normal case.

preserves.behavior: A finished PR still merges hands-free once declared complete - the fix must not add ceremony to the common case
Soundness-path PRs keep their existing withhold-and-revoke behaviour

work_units.evidence: DECIDED by Joe 2026-08-04: pr-open withholds, pr-ready arms. Established first that no local check can prevent this - in all three strandings (#1503, #1521, #1531) the working tree was clean at pr-open time and the extra commit came later from review feedback, and auto-merge-on-open.yml reacts to synchronize but the merge can complete before that push exists. So the only real prevention is to stop arming at creation. Hands-free is preserved two ways: 'make pr-ready' for a branch declared final, and 'make pr-open READY=1' to open and arm in one step. Rejected: HOLD=1 opt-out (prevents nothing by default, and only helps when you already know you are mid-work - exactly what I got wrong all three times) and detection-only (leaves the recovery cost in place).
work_units.summary: Pick the enablement point and confirm it keeps finished PRs hands-free

work_units.evidence: Makefile: pr-open no longer calls gh pr merge; it prints how to arm. New pr-arm-auto-merge holds the single arming implementation, consulted by both entry points, so the soundness withhold cannot drift between copies - verified 'gh pr merge --auto --squash' appears exactly once in the Makefile. New pr-ready delegates to it. Both targets added to .PHONY and confirmed to resolve via make -n. docs/operations/dev-loop-worktree-pool.md and repo-admin-settings.md updated so the documented flow matches.

tests/unit/workflows/test_auto_merge_enablement_point.py: 4 tests - pr-open does not arm directly, a hands-free path still exists (pr-ready plus READY=1), exactly one arming implementation, and (must-preserve) the arming path consults auto_merge_soundness_paths.py BEFORE arming so soundness withholding survives the move. Falsified against the pre-change Makefile: 3 of 4 fail, including 'pr-open arms auto-merge directly, so a PR can merge before a later commit is pushed'. tests/unit -k auto_merge: 47 passed; tests/unit/workflows: 138 passed.
